column1: # Known-answer vectors for the YMSG v9 "0x0b" auth crypt, consumed by YmsgCryptTests.
# These are NOT outputs of VintageHive's own code. They were produced by compiling the reference C
# implementation - yahoo_process_auth_0x0b() in bitlbee 1.2.4 protocols/yahoo/libyahoo2.c, plus that tree's
# md5.c, sha1.c, crypt.c, base64.c and yahoo_fn.c - into a small harness and running it. That code is GPL and
# VintageHive is MIT, so it is deliberately NOT vendored here; only these generated values are, and the port in
# Proxy/Yahoo/YmsgCrypt.cs is original code checked against them.
# To regenerate: fetch those files from the bitlbee 1.2.4 tree, wrap ymsg_auth_0x0b(seed, password) so it prints
# resp_6 and resp_96, and run it over the seeds below. Two things must hold for a seed to be usable as a vector,
# and both were verified for every row here:
#   1. the decode fills all 20 comparison bytes, and
#   2. it never reads past the parsed seed data
# A seed failing either makes the reference read uninitialised stack, so its output is not a stable answer to
# pin. Screening for this is why the seeds look arbitrary rather than tidy.
